prompt: Review PR 933 for the Trailhead project tracker, a small Node.js REST API. The change updates list endpoints from offset navigation to cursor navigation, along with the API documentation and tests. I need a review before this goes out because several clients and the command-line tool consume these collections, and the documented contract matters during the transition. Read the project and the PR materials in `pr/933/`, then write the review to `REVIEW.md` at the top of the project. Keep findings tied to the code or contract and explain the concrete impact. End the review with a fenced json list of findings, each with `location` (`path/to/file.ext:LINE`, using line numbers of the file as it is in the project), `severity` (critical, high, medium, low or nit), `issue` and `fix`.

rubric.criterion: Each important finding explains the concrete consequence in this project and gives a fix a developer can act on, without invented problems. Fail: generic findings ("add validation", "consider security"), or a finding the packet does not support. Partial: findings are grounded in the packet but some lack an actionable fix or a concrete consequence. Pass: every important finding names the place, the concrete consequence in this project and a fix a developer can build, and no finding is invented. (code cannot check this because it cannot judge whether an explanation is concrete or whether a proposed fix fits the project)

findingsKey.finding: The next cursor is encoded from the last row while the next query includes that row with a greater-or-equal comparison, so every non-final page repeats its last item.
Sorting only by createdAt leaves equal-time rows without a deterministic order, so inserts or store order changes can make cursor pages skip or repeat issues.
The cursor is merely base64 text containing an internal row offset, so clients can decode and alter it to request arbitrary positions rather than using a validated opaque continuation token.
The handler accepts any positive limit and never applies the configured or documented maximum of 100, allowing an unbounded response from a public list endpoint.
The change replaces the documented v1 top-level issues and nextOffset fields with a data/page envelope without moving the breaking contract to a new version or negotiated media type.

The new handler reads cursor but no longer reads the documented offset parameter, so existing clients receive the first page during the promised deprecation window instead of being migrated or supported.
